notes: Prologue machine ladder, 2009Q1–2016Q4. Follows Act I's machines.json field names (id, name, coin, available_from, hashrate_*, power_kw, price_new/price_used by quarter). Prices are USD per complete working unit. Player's PC is owned at start (no purchase). antminer_s9 price ramps down into Act I's own s9 entry (2017Q1 price_new $1,300) so the handover is seamless — do not duplicate s9 as a new model in Act I; reuse Act I's 's9' id from 2017Q1 onward and use this file's 2016 quarters only pre-handover.

models.name: Your Gaming PC (CPU)
models.real_basis: Consumer Core 2 Duo/early Core i-series desktop CPU mining SHA-256 in CPU miner software (2009-2010)
models.why: The only thing anyone mined with before GPU miners existed (Oct 2010). Already owned — no purchase.

hashrate_mhs.source: ≈ Core 2 Duo era; Bitcoin Wiki 'Non-specialized hardware comparison' gives a Nehalem i7-920 at ~40 MH/s @130W — a mid-2009 dual-core is well below that

power_kw.source: ≈ typical Core 2 Duo-class desktop under load

noise_db.source: ≈ a normal desktop tower, stock cooler

models.price_source: Free — the player already owns this PC at prologue start (doc 23 §3).

models.name: Gaming GPU (Radeon HD 5870-class)
models.real_basis: AMD Radeon HD 5870 (launched 23 Sep 2009, widely used for SHA-256 mining from mid-2010 once OpenCL miners matured)
models.why: The card that made GPU mining make sense: VLIW5 shader architecture was unusually good at the bitwise SHA-256 workload.

hashrate_mhs.source: Bitcoin Wiki 'Non-specialized hardware comparison' / community OpenCL miner benchmarks, HD 5870 ~380-393 MH/s

models.price_source: Launch price $399 (TechSpot); used/decline path estimated from typical GPU depreciation as ASICs arrived (no dated resale-price series found — estimate).

models.name: FPGA Mining Board
models.real_basis: ZTEX USB-FPGA Module 1.15x (single Xilinx Spartan-6 LX150)
models.why: A brief efficient middle step between GPUs and ASICs — far less power for the same hashrate, but expensive and fiddly (bitstream flashing, no plug-and-play miner software).

hashrate_mhs.source: Bitcoin Wiki 'ZTEX FPGA Boards for Bitcoin Mining'

models.price_source: ≈ aggregator listing ~$400-460 for ZTEX 1.15x; low confidence, niche product with thin price data.
models.notes: Quad-FPGA variant (ZTEX 1.15y, ~4x hashrate/power) exists in the real record but is left out of the alpha for simplicity; use this single-board model scaled by quantity if a bigger jump is wanted.

models.name: Early ASIC (pre-order)
models.real_basis: Composite of Avalon Batch 1 (on-time outlier) and Butterfly Labs Jalapeno/Single SC (the norm: severe delay)
models.why: The gamble that defines this era: pay now, hope it arrives before difficulty eats the profit.

hashrate_ghs.source: Avalon Batch 1 spec, Bitcoin Magazine 'Avalon Ships Bitcoin's First Consumer ASICs'

efficiency_j_per_gh.source: Bitcoin Wiki Avalon1 gives ~6.6 J/GH on-chip; 10 J/GH at-the-wall is closer to typical real draw

models.price_source: Avalon Batch 1 sold at $1,299 (Jan 2013); Batch 2 at $1,499 (Bitcoin Magazine). Delivery risk is resolved separately by preorders.json, not by this price table.
models.notes: This model id is used for the in-game invented vendor's pre-order card; the unit itself is Avalon-class hardware, the DELAY is Butterfly-Labs-class (see preorders.json).

models.why: Sets up Act I's GPU-rig story: this is a different, earlier card than Act I's gpu_gen1 (RX 580, 2017+), reflecting that ETH mining hardware moved fast even before the 2017 boom.
